issues.description: Field Farm.animals: the problem statement (UML and text) requires the farm to use a List<Animal> and specifically instructs to implement it using an ArrayList initialized in the no-arg constructor. The reference solution instead declares a field of type Queue<Animal> and initializes it with new LinkedList<>(), and its getter/setter use Queue<Animal>. This type mismatch between the specified attribute type (List/ArrayList) and the solution's attribute type (Queue/LinkedList) can confuse students about the expected field type and the required getter/setter signatures and may cause tests or student implementations that follow the specification to diverge from the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix:
Make the collection type consistent. Preferred fixes:
1) Change the reference solution to match the problem statement: declare the field as 'private List<Animal> animals;' (import java.util.List;), initialize it in the no-arg constructor with 'this.animals = new ArrayList<>();' and update getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal>. OR
2) If using a Queue/LinkedList is intentional, update the problem statement and UML to not mandate ArrayList/List and instead describe the collection more generically (e.g., "a collection of animals (any List or Queue implementation)"). Prefer option (1) to preserve the current exercise instructions that explicitly ask for List/ArrayList.
